I am 62 years old and have been farming these lands in Quzhou County for forty years. I finished middle school, so I can read the instructions on seed bags and fertilizer packets, and I know how to calculate costs. My household has just my wife and me—our children have left for the city. My wife does some part-time work at a nearby factory, so most days I am the one in the fields. With only two of us, I cannot afford to take big risks or spread myself too thin. I have a well for irrigation, which gives me some control when the rain does not come, but electricity costs money, so I count every pump.

I have 10.1 mu total. The main rotation is wheat–maize, which I run on 8.0 mu. That is my bread and butter. The remaining 2.1 mu I plant with cotton. Cotton brings good money when the price is right, but it is heavy on labor and sprays. With only two of us, 2.1 mu is about as much cotton as I can manage without hiring help, and hired labor now costs more than 150 yuan per day.

For the winter wheat on the 8.0 mu: I will buy improved seed from the county supply store—about 30 jin per mu. I learned my lesson years ago about cheap market seed. After the maize comes off in late September, I will pass the rotary tiller once to break the stalks and level the field. I broadcast the seed and basal fertilizer together, then drag a plank to cover. I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. In March, if the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I topdress with urea—about 15 jin per mu. I will irrigate four times: a winter irrigation if the soil is too dry, once at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. Wheat pays the bills, so I do not skimp on water. For pests, I spray herbicide once after planting, insecticide twice in spring and early summer, and fungicide once if the humidity is high. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize on the same 8.0 mu: timing is everything. I plant hybrid seed within two days of wheat harvest in early June—any later and the autumn frost catches you. I buy the hybrid packages, about 1 package per mu. I put all the fertilizer in the furrow at planting—about 80 jin of compound per mu. There is no time for split application; the season is too short. I till as little as possible, maybe one quick pass if the ground is hard, then plant immediately. I irrigate twice if the summer is dry, though sometimes the July rains help. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for corn borer. I expect around 500 kg per mu.

For the cotton on the 2.1 mu: I rotary till in mid-to-late April when the soil warms up. I plant improved cotton seed, about 3 jin per mu. I spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. Cotton needs careful water management—I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage, but I am careful not to overwater or the bolls will rot. The real headache is insects. Bollworm, aphids, mites—I have to spray about 12 times through the season. I also spray herbicide once. It is a lot of work walking the sprayer, but on 2.1 mu I can just manage it myself. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu if I stay on top of the pests.

My wife’s off-farm income helps with household costs, but I try to cover the farm inputs from farm sales. I do not hire labor—on 10.1 mu with only three crops, I and my wife can handle it if I plan carefully. My total costs run higher because of the cotton sprays, but cotton prices have been decent, so it balances out.
